questions.stem: Which part of the body does a supraclavicular brachial plexus block usually cover?
options: Arm and hand only, never the shoulder
Lower limb from the hip down
Whole upper limb, often including the shoulder

questions.stem: Which skin area is never covered by any brachial plexus technique for supraclavicular block?
questions.answer: Proximal medial arm skin (intercostobrachial nerve, T2)

questions.stem: For which surgery is a supraclavicular brachial plexus block suited?
options: Surgery from mid-humerus down to the hand

questions.stem: How suitable is a supraclavicular block for shoulder analgesia?
options: First choice, the most reliable option

questions.stem: Why was supraclavicular block unpopular before ultrasound was available?
Why is supraclavicular block considered the most extensive and reliable brachial plexus approach?
options: It is performed only under general anaesthesia
The trunks run far apart at this level
Trunks and divisions are tightly packed over the first rib
It avoids any risk to the pleura

questions.stem: What is the most common serious complication of supraclavicular block?
Pneumothorax after supraclavicular block occurs in about ____ with paraesthesia or nerve stimulator techniques.
What incidence of phrenic nerve paresis is reported after supraclavicular block?
Where should the needle tip lie in a supraclavicular block?
options: Within the pleural space, deep to the first rib
Inside the plexus sheath, posterior and superficial to the subclavian artery

questions.stem: Which direction is the in-plane needle approach for supraclavicular block?
What may be felt when the needle enters the plexus sheath in supraclavicular block?
How many injection sites are usually used for a supraclavicular block?
Which nerves does the corner pocket injection in supraclavicular block target?
Between which trunks is the second injection site in supraclavicular block placed?
In supraclavicular block, what should you do if the plexus moves away during a 1–2 mL injection?
options: Advance 1–2 mm closer to the plexus
Withdraw the needle 5 cm at once

questions.stem: For which patients have lower local anaesthetic volumes been suggested in supraclavicular block?
What needle length is used for supraclavicular block?
What total volume of local anaesthetic is typical for supraclavicular block?
What current and pulse width are used for nerve stimulation in supraclavicular block?
Which patient position is usual for supraclavicular block?
options: Supine, head of bed raised, head turned away, arm adducted
Standing, head flexed forward, arm abducted

questions.stem: What is placed under the scapula in supraclavicular block positioning, and why?
questions.answer: A bump, to create working space

questions.stem: Why ask the patient to reach for the ipsilateral knee during supraclavicular block?
questions.answer: Depresses the clavicle and opens the anterolateral neck

questions.stem: For a left supraclavicular block, which way should the operator face?
Where is the linear probe placed for supraclavicular block ultrasound?
questions.answer: Transverse, just above the clavicle at its midpoint

questions.stem: How does the subclavian artery look in cross-section on ultrasound in supraclavicular block?
How does the first rib look on ultrasound in supraclavicular block?
questions.answer: Linear hyperechoic line with an anechoic shadow beneath

questions.stem: What confirms that a hyperechoic line is the pleura during supraclavicular block ultrasound?
How does the brachial plexus appear on ultrasound in supraclavicular block?
questions.answer: Cluster of hypoechoic ovals, a bunch of grapes

questions.stem: How many clusters does the plexus often show on ultrasound in supraclavicular block?
Which roots form the superficial, lateral plexus clusters seen in supraclavicular block?
Which roots form the deep, medial plexus cluster seen in supraclavicular block?
Which artery often runs through or near the plexus and should be found with colour Doppler?
What are the three phases of continuous supraclavicular catheter placement?
questions.answer: Needle placement, catheter advancement, securing the catheter

questions.stem: Which steps does ultrasound guide in most patients for a continuous supraclavicular block?
In continuous supraclavicular block, where should the needle tip sit before piercing the sheath?
What are the downsides of tunnelling a supraclavicular catheter?
What is a typical starting infusion for a continuous supraclavicular block?
What patient-controlled bolus volume is suggested hourly with a continuous supraclavicular infusion?
Which other catheter technique is described for continuous supraclavicular block?
Where should the catheter tip lie in a continuous supraclavicular block?
questions.answer: Near the trunks and divisions, beside the subclavian artery

questions.stem: Which part of the plexus is commonly spared by a supraclavicular block?
In supraclavicular block, failure to start injection at an opening pressure below ____ psi may mean intrafascicular injection.
Supraclavicular block ultrasound uses a linear transducer of ____ MHz.
